First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. Second, all recording files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not published openly or stored elsewhere. Third, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention is not permitted. 1. From Ms. Patel: Only the eight students who completed media-ethics training (J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20) may conduct recorded interviews, and we need a training-verification record in the approval file.

3. From Ms. Romero: Personal phones are out — we use district tablets instead. All files go in the restricted OralHistory drive, not openly published. Recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — no indefinite retention. And we need a secure-storage configuration record documenting these safeguards.

Should the remaining recordings still go on the public school website, or should we reconsider that given the storage requirements Ms. Romero outlined? I want to make sure we're all aligned.
